Summary:
The blog post reports on the AI-safety-focused parts of OpenAI’s 2016 “Self-Organising Conference on Machine Learning”. It summarises discussions on value alignment, interpretability/right-to-explanation, adversarial examples, and dual-use concerns. Each topic contains a chain of claims (risks → analytical problems → insights → design ideas → concrete mechanisms → empirical or anecdotal evidence) and implicitly suggests concrete interventions such as approval-directed agents, quantilisers, local explanation testing with LIME, adversarial training, and multi-stakeholder oversight for dual-use releases.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[83]  
Inference strategy justification: The source is conversational, so moderate inference (edge confidence 2) was used to make implicit design rationales, mechanisms and interventions explicit.  
Extraction completeness: All four top-level risks mentioned are traced through intermediate reasoning to at least one actionable intervention, with cross-links where discussions overlap (e.g. value alignment threads share nodes). No nodes remain isolated, and framework names (e.g. “quantilisers”) are decomposed into white-box components.  
Key limitations: 1) Sparse quantitative evidence limited some edge strengths to “medium/weak”. 2) Section titles were informal; “discussion on X” placeholders were used. 3) Some mechanisms (e.g. adversarial training efficacy) are inferred rather than explicitly stated.
